native_title: Rational-point undecidability for smooth projective varieties over the rational numbers
companion_title: A conditional coefficient-prime repair of the five-point height argument
main_abstract_original_TeX:
Combining OpenAI's negative solution of rational Hilbert's tenth problem
with Poonen's established effective transfer, we obtain undecidability of
rational-point existence for arbitrary smooth projective geometrically
integral varieties over $\Q$. We specify a homogeneous-equation input
promise and reconstruct the terminating contradiction algorithm. There is
also no computable uniform bound on the height of one rational point in
terms of the size of the presented equations. The arithmetic input is used
with two explicit corrections documented here and in the accompanying
verification supplement. This is a geometric consequence of that input;
neither the geometric reduction nor the base undecidability theorem is
claimed as a new independent solution.
companion_abstract_original_TeX:
We reconstruct the non-CM arithmetic part of the five-point height argument
in the pinned source \cite{Pinned}, replacing its new unrestricted
$2$-adic modularity input by Pan's published theorem at $5$.
The $2$-adic member of the resulting system supplies the conductor at $5$.
The deduction is conditional on the preceding geometric and height-comparison
inputs stated below; it neither certifies the entire upstream manuscript nor
establishes undecidability of rational polynomial solvability.
native_description_whole_original: Combining OpenAI's negative solution of rational Hilbert's tenth problem, with two explicit proof corrections documented in the verification package, and Poonen's established effective transfer, this note proves undecidability of rational-point existence for arbitrary smooth projective geometrically integral varieties over Q. It specifies homogeneous-equation presentations and valid-input oracle use, and rules out a computable uniform bound on the height of one point in terms of presentation size. Dimension and all size parameters may vary. The arithmetic breakthrough is attributed to OpenAI and the geometric reduction to Poonen; no independent solution of rational Hilbert's tenth problem, new geometric reduction, fixed-dimensional theorem, many-one hardness or first-priority claim is made. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and adversarial verification. The preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing at publication; no complete formal verification is claimed. The standalone height supplement explicitly states its retained geometric inputs.

main_claim: No algorithm decides rational-point existence on every valid homogeneous-equation presentation of a smooth projective geometrically integral variety over Q; ambient dimension, dimension, degrees, equation count and coefficient heights are unbounded. Derived from credited Poonen transfer and the explicitly corrected pinned OpenAI arithmetic input.
height_claim: No total computable B(s(e)) bounds the least primitive-coordinate height of one rational point whenever points exist; the input is the presentation and embedding, not an abstract isomorphism class.
geometric_reduction: Finite nonadaptive disjunctive valid oracle queries; no many-one, dimension-preservation, fixed-curve, fixed-surface, fixed-dimension, Fano/general-type/finite-point extension or first-priority claim.
dependency_credit: Poonen2009; earlier Q-case route to R. Robinson through Smorynski credited by Poonen; OpenAI H10 and pointwise 2-converse preprints at adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a; new arithmetic preprints unrefereed, no independent H10 solution or full formal/kernel verification.
technical_substitutions: Coefficient primes (5,2): Pan published modularity at 5, same-form 2-adic constituent controls conductor at 5; retains preceding geometric and height inputs.
Universal integral group-ring correction reconciles inverse/direct Frobenius-Euler and smoothing conventions before character evaluation; no factor of two per auxiliary prime.
companion_conditional_inputs: Fixed proper cover and principally polarized abelian-surface family with bounded defining field and reduction control.
Fixed discriminant-210 quaternionic non-CM/CM dichotomy, with retained uniform CM Faltings-height bound.
companion_fixed_configuration: Five individual rational branch values of the fixed discriminant-210 quotient, involution labels 30,42,70,105,210; not arbitrary five rational points.
companion_bound: Assuming those three inputs, h(s) <= H M_S(s)^c for s outside the five branch values; M_S is the product of primes outside fixed S with at least one odd contact order.
